extracted.intended_audience: researchers preparing NIH-style microbiology/genomics grant proposals and grant reviewers (microbial pathogenesis, comparative genomics)
extracted.subtask_description: Writing or evaluating an NIH-style Research Strategy (Significance, Innovation, Approach) for a microbiology/genomics proposal that uses comparative genomics, evolutionary analyses, RNA-seq, and transposon screens to identify metabolic pathways important to Coxiella burnetii intracellular growth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance
rubrics_metrics.description: Importance of the problem: Coxiella burnetii is the etiological agent of Q fever, can cause chronic disease with high mortality, is a select agent, and its biology/virulence mechanisms are poorly understood; a critical barrier is lack of knowledge about metabolic processes vital to intracellular growth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewer/producer should explain how the project will (1) uncover evolutionary history, (2) identify metabolic processes critical to intracellular growth, (3) improve basic physiology knowledge, (4) provide potential therapeutic targets, (5) provide a model approach applicable to other pathogens, and (6) examine specific hypotheses (e.g., importance of heme biosynthesis and tRNA acquisition). Show epidemiological and clinical relevance (e.g., disease burden, treatment limitations, antibiotic resistance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Innovation
rubrics_metrics.description: How the proposed research seeks to shift current research paradigms: current work is biased toward entry and host manipulation, leaving intracellular metabolism under-explored.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate novelty by (1) using a novel evolutionary-genomics approach to identify metabolic genes important for intracellular growth, (2) addressing an underexplored Stage 2 (intracellular metabolism), (3) hypothesizing HGT-driven emergence of virulence, (4) offering new therapeutic targets, and (5) revealing novel mechanisms (e.g., tRNA-acquisition-based virulence). Explicitly state how proposed methods/ideas overcome limitations of existing approaches (e.g., limitations of transposon screens and targeted deletions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Approach — Specific Aim 1: Identify pathogen-specific metabolic pathways
rubrics_metrics.description: Aim 1: sequence genome of Coxiella from Ornithodoros rostratus and perform comparative genomics to identify metabolic pathways exclusive to C. burnetii.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide background/justification that tick-associated Coxiella are avirulent and differ metabolically. Describe stepwise Research Design: (1) sequence, assemble and annotate the genome, (2) align to existing C. burnetii genomes using Mauve, (3) perform reciprocal BLAST to identify pathogen-specific genes, (4) use GO/DAVID/KEGG/MetaCyc to assign genes to metabolic pathways. State expected outcomes (complete genome, list of pathogen-specific genes/pathways) and training/mentoring plans for students who will perform bioinformatics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Genome sequencing, assembly and annotation standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards and methods for generating the Coxiella genome assembly and annotation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify sequencing platform and read type (Illumina NextSeq, 300-cycle paired-end), target DNA amount (~1 µg), assemblers (Velvet, IDBA), gap closure by PCR and Sanger sequencing, annotation via NCBI Prokaryotic Genome Annotation Pipeline with manual curation, and deposit final genome in GenBank with raw reads made publicly available. Include contingency plans for low pathogen-read fraction (resequencing) and for repeats (mate-pair or PacBio long reads).

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparative genomics to identify pathogen-specific metabolic genes
rubrics_metrics.description: Methods and criteria to detect genes/pathways present in pathogenic C. burnetii but absent in tick-associated Coxiella.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use whole-genome alignment (Mauve) against seven C. burnetii genomes and reciprocal BLAST to define pathogen-specific genes (genes without orthologs in tick-associated strains). Identify genes conserved across pathogenic strains. Map genes to metabolic pathways using GO, DAVID, KEGG, and MetaCyc. Emphasize identification at the pathway level (less vulnerable to misannotation of individual genes).

rubrics_metrics.name: Potential problems and alternative strategies (Aim 1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Anticipated technical obstacles for genome sequencing/assembly/annotation and corresponding alternatives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anticipate: (1) high proportion of tick DNA — solution: resequence additional Illumina lane to increase reads; (2) fragmented assembly due to repeats — solution: PCR/Sanger gap closure or resequence with Illumina mate-pair or PacBio for long reads; (3) inability to assign all genes to pathways — mitigation: focus on pathway-level identification rather than individual genes so incomplete functional assignments won't derail the aim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approach — Specific Aim 2: Define metabolic pathways critical to intracellular growth
rubrics_metrics.description: Aim 2: identify horizontally acquired (HGT) genes and pathogen-specific pathways, analyze expression in host cells, and validate functional importance using transposon-insertion libraries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Outline a three-part plan: (1) comprehensive evolutionary analysis to detect foreign-origin genes, (2) map HGT genes to metabolic pathways and compare to pathogen-specific pathways from Aim 1 to prioritize candidates, (3) validate with RNA-seq of C. burnetii during infection of human macrophages and with available Tn-insertion mutants. State that construction of targeted deletions is challenging, so use Tn mutants (including partial-loss insertions) as alternative validation.

rubrics_metrics.name: HGT detection criteria and methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Criteria and analytic methods to identify horizontally acquired genes in C. burnetii.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine parametric methods (G+C ratio, oligonucleotide frequency, codon usage) and phylogenetic methods (genes with phylogenies inconsistent with organismal history). Orthology cutoffs used in prior work: minimum 70% coverage and 30% amino-acid identity for BLAST-based ortholog detection. Tools/workflow: align with MUSCLE, mask with Gblocks, infer phylogenies with RAxML and PhyloBayes, and implement parametric detection with in-house PERL/PYTHON scripts. Provide statistical comparisons (e.g., GC and codon-adaptation index differences) to support HGT claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Validation using RNA-seq and transposon-insertion mutants
rubrics_metrics.description: Experimental validation of pathway importance during intracellular growth using gene expression profiling and functional mutant screens.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan RNA-seq experiments in THP-1-derived macrophages infected at MOI 25, collect total RNA at 3, 5, and 7 days post infection from three biological replicates, prepare Illumina mRNA libraries, sequence on NextSeq, and compare expression to C. burnetii grown in ACCM-2 controls. For functional evidence, screen transposon-insertion libraries for mutants with partial loss-of-function (since insertions in essential metabolic genes may be lethal); use existing Tn mutants (example: hemL insertion near 3' end reduces intracellular growth) from collaborators if available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritization criteria for validation and therapeutics targeting
rubrics_metrics.description: How candidate pathways/genes will be prioritized for follow-up and therapeutic targeting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize: (1) pathways synthesizing metabolites C. burnetii cannot obtain from host (e.g., heme, biotin), (2) pathways for metabolizing critical nutrients such as glutamate, and (3) proteins required for homeostasis (e.g., Na+/H+ antiporters). Emphasize non-redundant proteins in critical pathways (e.g., HemA and HemL) as ideal drug targets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary data and feasibility demonstration
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirement to demonstrate prior experience and preliminary results that support feasibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present prior publications and preliminary datasets (e.g., previously sequenced Coxiella genomes, RNA-seq experience, detection of putatively HGT-derived genes), provide concrete examples and metrics (e.g., assembled genome from ~5% pathogen reads in earlier work), and identify trainees who will perform analyses. Use preliminary phenotypic data (e.g., Tn-hemL growth reduction) as proof of concept.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data sharing and resource dissemination
rubrics_metrics.description: Commitments for data deposition and community resource sharing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State plans to deposit the assembled genome in GenBank and make raw sequencing reads publicly available. Highlight that generated genomic resources will be valuable for other investigators studying pathogen evolution and could enable broader comparative studies.
